title: Credit Administration Standard — Operating Credit Leverage and the Post-Split Limit on Farm Real Estate Loans
content:
**Standard.** When a member asks to split the farmstead out of a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage, the post-split limit — the largest principal, as a percentage of value, allowed on the loan after the split — is lowered for an operation leaning on its operating credit: when the member holds an operating line in active status drawn above 75 percent of its commitment and no operating line in suspended or matured status, it is 5.0 points lower; when the member holds an operating line in suspended or matured status, it is 10.0 points lower; otherwise it is not changed.

**What the records show.** The member's Operating Lines of Credit records: each line's status (active, suspended, matured or other), its outstanding principal and its commitment. A line's draw is its outstanding principal divided by its commitment, as a percentage.

## Ladder

| Member's Operating Lines of Credit | Change to the post-split limit |
|---|---|
| Any line in suspended or matured status | 10.0 points lower |
| No line suspended or matured; a line in active status drawn above 75 percent of its commitment | 5.0 points lower |
| No line suspended or matured; no active line drawn above 75 percent | no change |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical lines)

| Active line: outstanding principal against commitment | Any line suspended or matured | Draw | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 300000 of 400000 | no | 75.00 percent (not above 75) | no change |
| 300400 of 400000 | no | 75.10 percent | 5.0 points lower |
| 100000 of 400000 | yes | 25.00 percent | 10.0 points lower |
| none active | yes (a matured line) | — | 10.0 points lower |

On a product whose largest principal after a release is 70 percent, a 5.0-point reduction makes the post-split limit 65 percent, and a 10.0-point reduction makes it 60 percent.
